record.label: Corrected weighted finite-tree estimate with explicit hypotheses
record.locator: 07-positive-temperature.tex:211–450; EAMS arXiv:2111.06813v2 Proposition 2.1 and Lemmas 3.2–3.4,4.2–4.3; long §11.1
record.statement: In the specified EAMS one-step-lag recursion on a k-regular tree, k>=2, fix delta>0 and finite L>=1 with L*delta<1. Use iid Gaussian labels and the common node/cavity initial state sqrt(delta)*g_i. At the finitely many mesh times, assume |a_k|<=K>=1, spatial Lipschitz constants La,Lb for a_k,b_k uniform in k, identical normalized a_k for node/cavity updates, and E[(A_(i->j)^r)^2]=1. Then |k*E[z_o^L*z_v^L]-2*sqrt(k-1)*delta*sum_(r=1)^(L-1) E[B_o^r]|<=C(K,La,Lb,delta,L), independently of k. The sum is empty when L=1.
record.boundary: Conditional ordinary reconstruction for the specified finite recursion, not a new formal theorem. The coefficient expectation uses the vertex law; its normalization uses the cavity law. Fixed-horizon and spatial-Lipschitz hypotheses are essential. The generic temporal-sign counterexample concerns auxiliary Theorem 4.1 as printed, not specialized positive-Parisi Proposition 4.7 or EAMS Theorem 1.7. No horizon-, temperature- or terminal-cutoff-uniform constant is claimed.

aligned_passages.text: **Source comparison for the finite weighted-tree formula.** This is an auxiliary check of the positive-temperature route. Readers continuing the circuit argument can go directly to [§11.1.1](#temperature-route-comparison) or [§11.2](#fixed-word-probability). The comparison here is with [El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke, arXiv:2111.06813v2, 3 February 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06813v2). Proposition 2.1 (p. 7) sums the adjacent-time term over $\ell=2,\ldots,L$. Applying Lemma 4.3, equation (4.6) (p. 14), replaces the expectation in that summand by the coefficient at $r=\ell-1$, so the resulting range is $r=1,\ldots,L-1$. The displayed ranges in (4.5) (p. 13) and (4.18) (p. 16) are instead $2,\ldots,L$. Separately, the same-time display (2.21) in Lemma 2.8 (p. 9) omits a factor $1/k$ that is present in its proof and in Proposition 2.1. The QAOA manuscript's Appendix A already uses the latter proposition, the reindexed sum and spatial Lipschitz bounds for both $a$ and $b$. The two following calculations establish the finite discrepancies and their precise scope. They do not compare formulae in the journal edition. **The test weights expose the missing factor.** Work on the $k$-regular tree, $k\ge2$, and let all initial labels $g_i$ be independent standard Gaussians. In particular, the adjacent vertices $o,v$ have distinct labels $g_o,g_v$. Set $u_i^0=u_{i\to j}^0=g_i$, $A_{i\to j}^{-1}=1$, and use constant algorithmic update functions $F_r=H_r=1$. These satisfy EAMS Assumption 2 and its later boundedness Assumption 3. For the auxiliary tests in Lemma 2.8 choose $Y_o^r=g_o$ and $\widetilde Y_v^r=g_v$ for every $r\ge0$. Each test is measurable with respect to its required initial-label sigma-field, and all moments are finite. The tests are separate from the constant update functions. At $t=1$, the recursion gives $$ u_o^1=k^{-1/2}\sum_{x\sim o}g_x,\qquad u_v^1=k^{-1/2}\sum_{y\sim v}g_y. $$ Hence $$ \mathbb E[u_o^1u_v^1g_og_v] =\frac1k\sum_{x\sim o,\,y\sim v}\mathbb E[g_xg_yg_og_v] =\frac1k. $$ Only $x=v,y=o$ survives. The printed right side of (2.21) is $\mathbb E[g_v^2g_o^2]=1$; multiplying it by $1/k$ agrees with the calculation. Both initial labels matter. With both test weights equal to one, both sides are zero; with just the neighbouring test omitted, the left side is an odd Gaussian moment and is again zero. A bounded version uses $Y_o^r=\operatorname{sgn}(g_o)$ and $\widetilde Y_v^r=\operatorname{sgn}(g_v)$. Only the same edge pair survives, so $$ \mathbb E[u_o^1u_v^1\operatorname{sgn}(g_o)\operatorname{sgn}(g_v)] =\frac1k(\mathbb E|g|)^2=\frac{2}{\pi k}, $$ whereas the printed right side is $2/\pi$. These tests are bounded and initial-label measurable. Both witnesses concern the auxiliary weighted identity; neither substitutes arbitrary test weights into a Parisi output theorem. **The shifted endpoint violates the printed uniform finite bound.** For a separate test retain the initial labels and set $$ \delta=\varepsilon=\frac14,\qquad L=2,\qquad b(t,x)=0, \qquad a(t,x)= \begin{cases} 1,&0\le t<3/8,\\ -1,&3/8\le t<1. \end{cases} $$ Use the source's actual initial states $x_i^0=x_{i\to j}^0=\sqrt\delta\,g_i$ and its definitions $A_{i\to j}^r=a(r\delta,x_{i\to j}^r)$, $B_i^r=a(r\delta,x_i^r)$. The state initialization has not been set to zero; it drops out of these coefficients because $a$ is independent of $x$. This fixed function is bounded by $K=1$, has spatial Lipschitz constant zero, and satisfies $a^2=1$, so all directed-edge normalizers are exactly one. The drift has Lipschitz constant $M=0$, and $L\delta=1/2\le1-\varepsilon$. It therefore meets the printed hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 and Assumptions 2–3. That finite theorem does not require temporal continuity or positivity of $a$. At the mesh points, $a_0=a_1=1$ and $a_2=-1$. Thus $$ u_i^2=\frac1{\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \sum_{w\sim i}\sum_{y\sim w,\,y\ne i}g_y, \qquad z_i^2=\sqrt\delta\,(u_i^1+u_i^2). $$ The equal-time covariances across the edge are zero. Each adjacent-time covariance is $\sqrt{k-1}/k$: exactly $k-1$ labels occur in both sums, and their product normalization is $k\sqrt{k-1}$. Therefore $$ k\mathbb E[z_o^2z_v^2]=2\delta\sqrt{k-1},\qquad \frac{k}{2\sqrt{k-1}}\mathbb E[z_o^2z_v^2]=\delta. $$ The target printed in (4.5) uses $a(2\delta,x_o^2)=-1$, so it is $-2\delta\sqrt{k-1}$. Its absolute error is $4\delta\sqrt{k-1}$, which is unbounded as $k\to\infty$ while all arguments of the claimed constant $C(M,K,\delta,\varepsilon)$ remain fixed. This refutes auxiliary Theorem 4.1 as printed. The example is not a Parisi curvature: it changes sign. Consequently it is not by itself a counterexample to the specialized assertion (4.18) in Proposition 4.7; the endpoint correction there comes from the exact proposition and reindexing explained above. Neither test refutes the main EAMS Theorem 1.7. **A finite estimate with the required hypotheses.** The source argument does provide a usable replacement. Fix $\delta>0$, $L\ge1$ and $L\delta<1$. Allow the coefficients $a_k,b_k$ to depend on degree, but require bounds independent of $k$ at the finitely many mesh times: $|a_k|\le K$ with $K\ge1$, and spatial Lipschitz constants $L_a,L_b$ for $a_k,b_k$. Use the original initialization and the same normalized function for node and directed-edge coefficients, with $\mathbb E(A_{i\to j}^r)^2=1$. Then $$ \left|k\mathbb E[z_o^Lz_v^L] -2\sqrt{k-1}\,\delta\sum_{r=1}^{L-1}\mathbb E B_o^r\right| \le C(K,L_a,L_b,\delta,L). $$ The constant is independent of $k$, and the sum is empty when $L=1$. The coefficient expectation on the right uses the vertex law; its normalization was defined using the directed-edge law. The following proof keeps the two laws distinct. It reconstructs the finite estimate from EAMS Proposition 2.1 and Lemmas 3.2–3.4 and 4.2–4.3; it is not a claim that changing an index alone repairs every hypothesis of the printed theorem. Put $D=k-1$. Conditional on the earlier cavity labels, the new message is centered Gaussian with variance $(\tau^r)^2$. Its recursion is $$ (\tau_{i\to j}^{r+1})^2=\frac1D \sum_{\substack{w\in\partial i\\w\ne j}}(A_{w\to i}^{r-1})^2(\tau_{w\to i}^r)^2, \qquad \tau^0=1. $$ This conditional Gaussianity gives $\Delta_r=\mathbb E[((\tau^r)^2-1)^2]\le V_r/D$, where $$ V_0=0,\qquad V_{r+1}=2K^4V_r+2(K^4+1). $$ Indeed, split the conditional-variance recursion into the average of $(A^{r-1})^2((\tau^r)^2-1)$ and the average of $(A^{r-1})^2-1$. Jensen bounds the first square, while independence of child cavities and exact coefficient normalization bound the second by a constant over $D$. The moment recursion also gives $\mathbb E(u_{i\to j}^r)^2\le K^{2r}$. Splitting off the missing neighbour as in the source gives $\mathbb E|u_i^r-u_{i\to j}^r|^2\le4K^{2r}/k$. Subtract the node and directed-edge Euler recursions. Their equal initial states and the drift Lipschitz bound give $$ \mathbb E|x_i^r-x_{i\to j}^r|^2\le d_r/k, \quad d_0=0,\qquad d_{r+1}=2(1+\delta L_b)^2d_r+8\delta K^{2(r+1)}. $$ The bound $\|B_i^r-A_{i\to j}^r\|_2\le L_a\sqrt{d_r/k}$ now uses spatial Lipschitzness of $a$. This property is invoked in the proof of EAMS Lemma 4.2 but omitted from the printed hypotheses of Theorem 4.1; it is available in the QAOA manuscript's compact-strip application. For $s=\ell-1$, the adjacent-time summand of Proposition 2.1 is $$ Q_s=\mathbb E[A_{v\to o}^{s-1}(u_{v\to o}^s)^2B_v^{s-1}B_o^s]. $$ Let $\mathcal G_{i\to j}^{r,+}$ be the labels within distance $r$ of $i$ in its cavity after removing edge $ij$. Condition on $\mathcal G_{v\to o}^{s-1,+}\vee\mathcal G_{o\to v}^{s,+}$. The three coefficient factors are measurable there: their vertex balls split into these two disjoint cavity balls. The newest layer driving $u_{v\to o}^s$ is outside this field; adding the initial label at $v$ to the source's minus field does not change the conditional law, since that message and its variance exclude that label. Conditioning therefore replaces $(u_{v\to o}^s)^2-1$ by $(\tau_{v\to o}^s)^2-1$. Its contribution is bounded by $K^3\sqrt{V_s/D}$. Replacing the two node coefficients by directed-edge coefficients then costs at most $K^2L_a(\sqrt{d_{s-1}}+\sqrt{d_s})/\sqrt k$. The two directed-edge trees are independent; exact normalization reduces their product expectation to $\mathbb E A_{o\to v}^s$. One final comparison with $\mathbb E B_o^s$ proves $$ |Q_s-\mathbb E B_o^s|\le\frac{C_s}{\sqrt D},\quad C_s=K^3\sqrt{V_s}+K^2L_a\sqrt{d_{s-1}} +(K^2+1)L_a\sqrt{d_s}. $$ For the same-time remainder in that proposition, $|R_\ell|\le K^{2\ell+2}$ by boundedness and Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence the asserted finite bound holds, for example, with $$ C=2\delta\sum_{s=1}^{L-1}C_s +\delta\sum_{\ell=1}^LK^{2\ell+2}. $$ No constant uniform in increasing horizon, temperature or terminal cutoff has been asserted. **Why the continuum value survives the correction.** The QAOA manuscript already checks the convergence and uniform boundedness of its finitely many degree-dependent normalizers, and supplies both spatial Lipschitz bounds, before taking the degree limit. Its limiting coefficient $m_r=c_{\delta,r}\mathbb E a(t_r,X_r^\delta)$ satisfies $|m_r|\le1$ by Cauchy–Schwarz and the definition of $c_{\delta,r}$. The shifted and corrected sums differ exactly by $$ \delta\sum_{r=2}^Lm_r-\delta\sum_{r=1}^{L-1}m_r =\delta(m_L-m_1),\qquad |\delta(m_L-m_1)|\le2\delta. $$ Thus the error in the printed unnormalized finite theorem can grow like $\sqrt{k}$ at fixed mesh even though the correction disappears in the subsequent normalized continuum limit. The fixed-temperature coupling and separate strong realization in the QAOA manuscript justify that limiting application. These checks neither reject nor independently certify the whole EAMS or QAOA theorem. [OpenAI (2026b), Appendix A][q-positive].
